sections.label: Zero Waste Masterplan and Bill
sections.summary: The Masterplan sets strategies and policies for a circular economy and Zero Waste Nation, with the Resource Sustainability Bill giving effect to its policies and targets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The Masterplan lays out our strategies and policies to close our resource loops via a circular economy approach and to achieve our vision of a Zero Waste Nation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The Resource Sustainability Bill will give effect to the policies and targets outlined in the Masterplan.

sections.label: IPCC report on global warming
sections.summary: The IPCC Special Report released last year states current rates of human activity may lead to 1.5°C of global warming above pre-industrial levels by as early as 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Special Report released last year, current rates of human activity may lead to 1.5°C of global warming above pre-industrial levels by as early as 2030.

sections.label: NewSand from incineration bottom ash
sections.summary: If NewSand can be mined from incineration bottom ash, Semakau can be saved and its useful life extended beyond 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: What more if NewSand can be "mined" from incineration bottom ash!

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We can then "save" Semakau and extend its useful life beyond 2035.

sections.label: Net benefit from e-waste recovery
sections.summary: Preliminary studies estimate that recovering and reusing materials from e-waste can reap Singapore a net benefit of $40 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Preliminary studies have estimated that if Singapore recovers and reuses materials from e-waste, we can reap a net benefit of $40 million.

sections.label: Singapore e-waste generation and recycling
sections.summary: Singapore generates about 60,000 tonnes of e-waste annually, yet very little is recycled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Singapore generates about 60,000 tonnes of e-waste annually, yet very little is recycled.

sections.label: Extended Producer Responsibility for e-waste
sections.summary: Precious metals like gold are thrown away, so the Extended Producer Responsibility approach to e-waste will be introduced by 2021 to ensure proper handling and extraction of resources.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Precious metals like gold are also being thrown away.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We will introduce the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) approach to e-waste by 2021, to ensure the proper handling and extraction of resources from e-waste.

sections.label: Plastics recycling rate drop
sections.summary: The plastics recycling rate, which hovered around 10%, dropped to 4% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: As a result, our plastics recycling rate, which hovered around 10%, dropped to 4% in 2018.

sections.label: Mandatory food waste segregation
sections.summary: From 2024, owners and occupiers of commercial and industrial premises generating large amounts of food waste must segregate it for treatment, and new large food waste generators must treat it onsite.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: From 2024, we will make it mandatory for the owners and occupiers of commercial and industrial premises which generate large amounts of food waste to segregate their food waste for treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We will also require owners and occupiers of new buildings which are expected to be large food waste generators to treat food waste onsite.

sections.label: Producer registration and PRS
sections.summary: Clause 8 requires producers to register with NEA to supply regulated products, and clause 12 requires large producers above prescribed thresholds to join a PRS before supplying regulated consumer products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Clause 8 requires producers, as defined in the Bill, to register with NEA in order to supply regulated products, and clause 12 requires large producers above prescribed thresholds to join a PRS before they can supply regulated consumer products.

sections.label: Threshold annual turnover $10 million
sections.summary: The threshold criteria will, for a start, be set at an annual turnover of above $10 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, the threshold criteria will, for a start, be set at an annual turnover of above $10 million.

sections.label: Resource Sustainability Bill strategy
sections.summary: The Resource Sustainability Bill is part of a strategy to close resource loops through a circular economy approach to mitigate and adapt to climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The Resource Sustainability Bill is an integral part of our strategy to close resource loops through a circular economy approach to mitigate and adapt to climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Not only will it contribute to environmental sustainability, it will also help to build up the three resiliences – climate, economic and resource.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Only by doing so can we create a sustainable Singapore of tomorrow and secure our collective future for our children.

sections.label: Zero Waste Masterplan landfill target
sections.summary: The Zero Waste Masterplan launched last week highlighted a goal to cut waste sent to the landfill by 30%.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Zero Waste Masterplan launched last week highlighted that we want to cut waste sent to the landfill by 30%.

sections.label: Resource Sustainability Bill waste management
sections.summary: The Resource Sustainability Bill aims to improve waste management and hold key waste producers accountable for reduction.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If everybody thinks tackling climate change is someone else's responsibility, then who will take responsibility?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Resource Sustainability Bill, which aims to improve waste management in Singapore and support businesses to reduce and recycle their waste, is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill does well to hold key producers of various types of waste accountable for waste management and reduction.

sections.label: E-scooter disposal next July
sections.summary: With UL2722-certified e-scooters effective next July, at least 80,000 PMDs will be disposed of in the coming year.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With UL2722-certified e-scooters coming into effect next July, at least 80,000 PMDs will be disposed of in the coming year.

sections.label: Sustainability education and Semakau Landfill
sections.summary: Plans to educate on new regulations were asked, and efforts to promote sustainability continue as Semakau Landfill may reach capacity in 16 years.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Do we have plans to educate them on these new regulations?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In English): We will continue to push on with more efforts to promote sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's only landfill, Semakau Landfill, is expected to reach capacity in just 16 years if we continue to generate waste at current rates.

sections.label: Plastic packaging waste increase
sections.summary: Plastic waste disposed rose from 540,800 tonnes in 2003 to 908,600 tonnes in 2018, a main source being packaging waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A main source of such packaging waste is made from plastic and, looking at the statistics over time, plastic waste disposed has gone way up from 540,800 tonnes in 2003 to 908,600 tonnes in 2018.

sections.label: Zero Waste Masterplan packaging producers
sections.summary: The Zero Waste Masterplan targets excessive packaging, initially aiming at packaged product producers and supermarkets with turnover over $10 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While it is not clear in the Bill itself, the Zero Waste Masterplan notes that the problem is on excessive packaging, and the initial aim of the framework is at producers of packaged products and supermarkets with a turnover of more than $10 million.

sections.label: Food loss cost study
sections.summary: The Singapore Environment Council study indicated food loss contributes an estimated $2.54 billion from farm to market within Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Environment Council (SEC) indicated in a recent study that food loss contributes to an estimated $2.54 billion from farm to market within Singapore.

sections.label: E-waste public collection prohibition
sections.summary: The Bill prohibits public e-waste collection unless operating a licensed scheme or with NEA written approval, with fines up to S$5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the provisions of the Bill, public collection of e-waste will henceforth be prohibited unless they are operating a licensed scheme or have a written approval of NEA to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Any person who does so will be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding S$5,000.

sections.label: Virogreen Thailand import licence suspension
sections.summary: Thailand suspended Virogreen's import licence for a year after 96 tonnes of e-waste labelled second-hand appliances entered its plants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A case in point is Singapore-based Virogreen which had their import licence suspended for a year by Thailand’s Department of Industrial Works after police investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This was due to a batch of cargo with 96 tonnes of e-waste that were labelled as second-hand electronic appliances from countries, including Singapore, which found its way, according to Thai media reports, into their e-waste management plants.

sections.label: Ban on primary micro plastic
sections.summary: The Member asks the Senior Minister of State to consider banning primary micro plastic production and use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To prevent more of such micro plastics from entering the environment and wrecking damage, I wish to ask the Senior Minister of State if she will consider a ban on primary micro plastic production and use.

sections.label: Pulau Semakau lifespan and waste volume
sections.summary: Pulau Semakau's 157-hectare plot holds about 6,680 pools of ash, with projected lifespan now 2035, 10 years earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The current 157-hectare plot that we are using in Pulau Semakau can hold approximately 6,680 Olympic-sized swimming pools worth of ash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Last year, before incineration, which reduces the volume by about 90%, we generated 15,000 Olympic-sized swimming pools of waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In fact, the current projected lifespan of Pulau Semakau is 2035, 10 years earlier from previous estimates and only about 16 years from now.

sections.label: Offence for non-individuals disposing regulated products
sections.summary: Clause 17 makes it an offence for non-individuals to dispose of regulated products as waste outside licensed schemes or approved collectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Furthermore, clause 17 makes it an offence for non-individuals to dispose of regulated products as waste instead of through the licensed producer responsibility scheme, licensed waste collector or licensed e-waste recycler, or someone approved to collect e-waste.

sections.label: Building managers food waste facility
sections.summary: Clause 26 requires building managers of certain buildings to provide their own food waste management facility within the premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 26 requires building managers of certain kinds of buildings to provide their own food waste management facility within the premises.

sections.label: Onsite food waste processing saves cost
sections.summary: Our Tampines Hub needs one garbage compactor truck daily instead of three, saving management about $40,000 annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While compelled by law to manage food waste, processing food waste onsite may actually save cost for management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is what happened in Our Tampines Hub (OTH) where only one garbage compactor truck is needed daily, compared to three previously, saving the management about $40,000 annually.

sections.label: Extending food waste management systems
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry plans to extend food waste management systems to residential estates or make facilities accessible to non-occupants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, since there is great benefit in composting food waste, does the Ministry have plans to extend food waste management systems to residential estates or make such food waste management facilities accessible to non-occupants of the prescribed building?

sections.label: Pulau Semakau landfill lifespan shortened
sections.summary: The only landfill at Pulau Semakau had its lifespan shortened from 2045 to 2035.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Already, our only landfill at Pulau Semakau had its lifespan shortened from 2045 to 2035.

sections.label: Waste reduction target for Semakau
sections.summary: The announced target is to reduce daily waste sent to Semakau by 30% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The target announced is to reduce the daily waste sent to Semakau by 30% by 2030.

sections.label: Export of recyclable waste
sections.summary: Singapore exports 30% of its recyclable waste to countries including Australia, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, South Korea and Thailand for processing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The other major problem is the fact that we export 30% of our recyclable waste to countries, including Australia, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, South Korea and Thailand for processing.

sections.label: SEC study on food waste
sections.summary: A recent SEC study shows one-fifth of total food in Singapore, over 390,000 tonnes of fresh produce, is wasted in the food supply chain.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The recent study by SEC shows that one-fifth of total food in Singapore, over 390,000 tonnes of fresh produce, is wasted in the food supply chain.

sections.label: Household food waste segregation pilot
sections.summary: The passage asks whether residential premises should be required to segregate food waste, citing a Tampines GreenLace pilot that collected 4,000 kg over three months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But given that half of the total food waste generated comes from residential households, should we not require the same undertaking for residential premises?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I understand from Minister Masagos' reply to my Parliamentary Question last month that a household food waste segregation pilot was conducted at Tampines GreenLace and the results were very promising, with 4,000 kilogrammes (kg) of food waste collected over three months.

sections.label: Domestic recycling rates stuck
sections.summary: Domestic recycling rates have remained stuck at 21%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Domestic recycling rates have remained stuck at 21%.

sections.label: Certified bags for waste disposal
sections.summary: The passage suggests mandating government-certified garbage bags and food waste bags to nudge households toward reducing plastic use and segregating food waste.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In some cities, authorities have mandated households to purchase and only use government-certified garbage bags for the disposal of thrash.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This nudges citizens to think less of convenience and more of the cost of convenience and leads to overall reduction in the use of plastic bags.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We could also consider nudging household food waste segregation by mandating the use of Government-certified food waste bags with printed diagrams of what would be considered food waste.

sections.label: Visible recycling and upstream food waste
sections.summary: The passage states that visible neighbour recycling encouraged social behaviour, and calls for attention to transnational waste streams and upstream food waste measures.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, residents were encouraged and nudged when they can visibly see their neighbour recycle, bumping into the green bags of recyclables at the lift lobby on collection days.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Neighbours can even gently correct recycling mistakes, since the bag was translucent.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It promoted recycling as social behaviour and collective action, which is always more effective than to try to change individual behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The focus on e-waste, packaging waste and food waste is also a correct focus.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, we need to pay attention to the growing transnational dimension of our waste streams to ensure our efforts do not go to waste.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We also need to go more upstream to tackle the problem of food waste, reducing loss in the food supply chain and recycling food waste for compost to improve local food production.

sections.label: Waste generation and landfill space
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore generated 7.7 million tonnes of solid waste in 2018, a 0.1% decrease, with food waste at 763,100 tonnes and landfill space running out in 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Closer to home, our waste generation has not reduced substantially at all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We generated 7.7 million tonnes of solid waste in 2018, only a 9,000 tonne or a dismal 0.1% decrease from the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, we generated 763,100 tonnes of food waste, accounting for 10% of our total waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At this rate, our landfill will run out of space in 2035.

sections.label: Food loss could feed vulnerable groups
sections.summary: The passage states that each person eats 1,095 daily meals a year, enough to feed about 390,000 people, and that yearly food loss could provide food security for vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Each person eats 1,095 daily meals a year, which is to say, we can safely feed about 390,000 people a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That means, Mr Deputy Speaker, this food loss every year could provide food security for all our vulnerable groups!

sections.label: Volunteers collect unsold fresh produce
sections.summary: Its volunteers collect 1,500 kg of unsold fresh produce weekly from Pasir Panjang Wholesale Centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Its volunteers collect a staggering 1,500 kg of unsold fresh produce once a week from Pasir Panjang Wholesale Centre.

sections.label: Lowest quintile food spending
sections.summary: Based on the Household Expenditure Survey 2017/2018, lowest quintile Singaporeans spend 49% of income on food.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on the Report on the Household Expenditure Survey 2017/2018, comparing the expenditures on food and income, excluding Central Provident Fund, of our lowest quintile Singaporeans, 49% of their income is spent on food.

sections.label: Meals programmes cost estimates
sections.summary: Close to $15 million could be redirected, based on estimates for Meals-on-Wheels and Willing Hearts providing over 10,000 daily meals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on our estimates on how much it costs for programmes like Meals-on-Wheels and Willing Hearts that provide more than 10,000 daily meals in total, close to $15 million could be redirected to other aspects of social support, especially as higher standards of living with higher temperatures mean that the basic needs of even our most vulnerable must also be constantly reviewed.

sections.label: National vision feeding 400,000
sections.summary: If SG Food Rescue can move hundreds of tonnes of food loss yearly, a national vision could feed all 400,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If a small group of citizen volunteers like SG Food Rescue can move hundreds of tonnes of food loss every year to where they are needed most, imagine what we can do if we – the Government, business and community – truly commit our will and resources to a national vision of getting all 400,000 people fed, and make climate change everyone's concern.

sections.label: Amazon fires rise
sections.summary: The Amazon has seen more than 80,000 fires this year, a 77% rise over the same period in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Amazon, a vital carbon store that slows down the pace of global warming, has seen more than 80,000 fires break out so far this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is a 77% rise, compared to the same period in 2018.

sections.label: Resource Sustainability Bill responsibility
sections.summary: The Resource Sustainability Bill places more responsibility on businesses and producers in the supply chain to reduce, reuse and recycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Resource Sustainability Bill is a good attempt to create a long-term solution to complement individual efforts in the 3Rs by placing more responsibility on businesses and producers in the supply chain to reduce, reuse and recycle.

sections.label: Short-term compliance costs
sections.summary: In the short term, companies could face increased compliance costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the short term, companies could face increased compliance costs.

sections.label: Sustainability and economic growth
sections.summary: The passage urges striving for sustainability, stating economic growth and sustainability are mutually reinforcing and beneficial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Let us continue to strive for sustainability, not only because of the world we wish our future generations to inherit, but because we believe we stand to reap the rewards for doing so in a very tangible way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Singapore Story is testament to our belief that economic growth and sustainability are themselves not mutually exclusive but are instead mutually reinforcing and beneficial.

sections.label: Food and e-waste statistics
sections.summary: Ministry statistics put food waste at 763 million kg and e-waste at 60 million kg per year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Statistics released by the Ministry places the amount of food waste per year at 763 million kg and the amount of e-waste per year at 60 million kg.

sections.label: In-store e-waste collection
sections.summary: Paragraph 15(1) states that large retailers must offer in-store collection of certain e-waste.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In relation to paragraph 15(1), it is stated that "large retailers must offer in-store collection of certain e-waste".

sections.label: Resource Recovery Infrastructure Fund
sections.summary: The Resource Recovery Infrastructure Fund aims to improve collection, sorting and recycling, with an estimated 900,000 tons less landfill waste yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In particular, one of the grants, known as the Resource Recovery Infrastructure Fund, aims to improve the collection, sorting and recycling of processed materials.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It has proven successful, with an estimated reduction in 900,000 tons of landfill waste per year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Third, the Government should set up an online National Registry of Producers and Regulated Products.

sections.label: Tax breaks for CSR
sections.summary: The Government can provide tax breaks or grants to retailers engaging in CSR programmes such as replacing energy-inefficient appliances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Second, the Government can provide tax breaks or grants to retailers who choose to engage in CSR programmes, such as replacing the energy-inefficient appliances of low-income households with more energy-efficient models.

sections.label: Supermarket food donation initiative
sections.summary: The Government can work with supermarkets so food nearing expiry goes to the less well-off, citing France's 2016 donation law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Third, the Government can work with our supermarkets to ensure that food nearing expiry is not simply disposed of but is provided to the less well-off in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The French Government passed a law in 2016 mandating that large supermarkets have to donate excess food to food banks and charitable organisations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: If we had a similar initiative in Singapore, we can not only reduce the amount of food waste, but we can also help those in need.

sections.label: Reinvent, recalibrate and reward
sections.summary: The speaker proposes requiring those who profit from products to collect and treat them when they become waste.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition to reduce, reuse and recycle, therefore, I propose that we strive to reinvent, recalibrate and reward.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By requiring that those who profit from the supply of products be responsible for collecting and treating these products when they become waste, companies will be more cognizant of downstream effects of their commercial activity.

sections.label: Planned obsolescence and repair rights
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to consider laws against planned obsolescence and to strengthen consumers' rights to repair products.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their phones are designed to last for at least five years, more than twice the standard 24-month smartphone replacement cycle.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition to the much-welcomed Resource Sustainability Act, therefore, I would like to ask the Minister to consider introducing additional laws to combat the exploitative practice of planned obsolescence, as well as laws to strengthen consumers' rights to repair their electrical and electronic products.

sections.label: Cutting disposable packaging items
sections.summary: Conference organisers, hotels and bakeries should stop goody bags, small toiletry bottles and individually wrapped buns; FairPrice is trialling plastic bag charges.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Conference organisers should dispense with goody bags, hotels can do away with small toiletry bottles and bakeries must discontinue this practice of wrapping buns in individual bags.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I was delighted to learn before entering the House today that FairPrice is starting a month-long trial to charge for plastic bags in various outlets.

sections.label: Food loss in Singapore
sections.summary: A SEC study on a circular food economy estimated $2.54 billion of food loss occurs in Singapore from farm to market annually.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the recent study by SEC on building a circular food economy revealed, an estimated $2.54 billion of food loss occurs in Singapore from farm to market annually.

sections.label: Rewarding green consumer choices
sections.summary: Schemes can reward consumers choosing smaller carbon footprint options with loyalty points, and rating and voting systems can reward green companies.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, on the consumer level, we can introduce schemes to change consumer behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Those who choose options with a smaller carbon footprint can be rewarded with loyalty points that translate into discounts.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, consumers can be encouraged to reward companies that offer more green alternatives through rating and voting systems.

sections.label: Resource Sustainability Bill waste streams
sections.summary: The Resource Sustainability Bill seeks to better manage electrical and electronic waste, packaging waste including plastics, and food waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Resource Sustainability Bill seeks to better manage three critical waste streams: electrical and electronic waste; packaging waste, including plastics; and food waste.

sections.label: E-waste producer responsibility organisation
sections.summary: Under the Bill, large-scale e-waste producers must fund a Producer Responsibility Organisation to organise e-waste collection and recycling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, e-waste, which encompasses electrical and electronic consumer equipment, large-scale producers are required to fund a Producer Responsibility Organisation (PRO) which will be responsible for organising e-waste collection and recycling.

sections.label: Singapore food waste growth
sections.summary: Food waste in Singapore grew by around 30% over the last 10 years, with 738 million kg generated in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, food waste has grown by around 30% over the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, 738 million kg of food waste was generated.

sections.label: Food waste minimisation guidebook
sections.summary: The Sustainable Singapore Blueprint 2015 aims to prevent and reduce food wastage at source, and NEA offers a Food Waste Minimisation Guidebook for Food Manufacturing Establishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the food waste management strategy laid out in the Sustainable Singapore Blueprint 2015, the key goal is to Prevent and Reduce Food Wastage at Source.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, a Food Waste Minimisation Guidebook for Food Manufacturing Establishments is now available from NEA to help businesses with this goal.

sections.label: Food waste segregation from 2024
sections.summary: From 2024, commercial and industrial premises generating large amounts of food waste must segregate and treat it on their premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, from 2024, commercial and industrial premises that generate large amounts of food waste must segregate and treat the food waste on their premises.

sections.label: Cold food chain infrastructure support
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister if there are plans to better support infrastructure for cold food chain management standards to reduce food loss and waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this context, may I ask the Minister if there are plans to better support the infrastructure for better standards in cold food chain management to reduce food loss and waste?

sections.label: Waste Bill and retailer costs
sections.summary: The Bill legislates ways to tackle e-waste, packaging waste and food waste, with collection services free to consumers but costs recovered through raised prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In concluding my speech, it is my heartfelt hope that with support from the Ministry, other TACs will all come together and work together with SMF in achieving a better future for our next generations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This Bill takes an important step towards greater sustainability for our environment in legislating better ways of tackling ever-increasing amounts of waste generated in Singapore, with the biggest groups being the ones targeted in this Bill, namely, e-waste, packaging waste and food waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Besides getting large retailers to offer in-store collection of certain e-waste and onsite collection upon deliveries to customers, the legislation also makes provisions for these services to be without charge to consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But the reality is that there is no free lunch in this world and the cost of labour and transportation will be included and recovered through sales, with prices increased across the board for retailers to remain viable as businesses.

sections.label: E-waste collection cost offsetting
sections.summary: The Bill stipulates that e-waste collectors may not charge for the service but offset costs by raising fees for other products and services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The Bill stipulates that companies which collect e-waste may not charge for this service but they will offset the cost of collection by raising fees for other products and services.

sections.label: E-waste recycling rates and EU targets
sections.summary: Only 6% of e-waste is recycled, and EU member states had to collect 45 tonnes per 100 tonnes from 2016, revised to 65 tonnes in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Only 6% or six tonnes of every 100 tonnes of e-waste are recycled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From 2016, EU member states had to collect 45 tonnes of e-waste for every 100 tonnes of electronic goods put on sale during the previous three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The target was revised up to 65 tonnes in 2019.

sections.label: Definition of large retailers
sections.summary: The Bill defines large retailers as retailers occupying premises with a floor area of 300 square metres or larger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, the Bill defines "large retailers" as retailers that occupy any premises with a floor area of 300 square metres (sqm) or larger.

sections.label: Reporting plans to reduce food waste
sections.summary: The question asks whether MEWR plans for businesses to report food waste reduction plans, similar to packaging producers submitting plans to NEA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Does MEWR have plans for businesses to also report their plans to reduce their food waste, similar to how producers of packaging and packaged products have to submit plans to NEA on how much packaging they put-to-market annually and, again, their plans to reduce, reuse and recycle packaging waste?

sections.label: Encouraging technology and packaging demand
sections.summary: The question asks if the Ministry will encourage businesses to adopt technology, noting continued packaging demand would make the packaging EPR futile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Beyond the reporting on how a business will reduce food waste, will the Ministry also consider encouraging businesses to adopt such technology?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If there is continued demand for packaging, then the EPR that we will introduce for packaging waste will be futile.

sections.label: Alternative plans to plastic bag charge
sections.summary: The speaker asks MEWR to share alternative plans if a plastic bag charge is not the way to go.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If MEWR feels that a plastic bag charge is not the way to go, then I hope they can share with this House what are the alternative plans.

sections.label: Zero Waste Masterplan targets
sections.summary: The Bill must be read with the Zero Waste Masterplan, which targets a 30% cut in per-capita landfill waste by 2030 and promotes a circular economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill has to be read in conjunction with the inaugural Zero Waste Masterplan, which sets a bold target to reduce per-capita landfill waste by 30% by 2030, while promoting the development of a circular economy that generates efficiencies from reducing and reusing waste.

sections.label: China scrap import ban
sections.summary: The Chinese government banned the import of all but the purest scrap material in 2017, killing a trade worth $24 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All this came to a halt when the Chinese government banned the import of all but the purest scrap material in 2017, killing a trade worth $24 billion a year." End quote.

sections.label: In-store collection facilities requirement
sections.summary: Section 15 provides that large retailers must offer in-store collection facilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, section 15 provides that large retailers must offer in-store collection facilities.

sections.label: Prepaid disposal fee on EEE
sections.summary: One possibility is imposing an appropriate, prepaid disposal fee on new EEE products at the point of sale in Singapore, regardless of how they are supplied.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One possibility is to impose the appropriate, prepaid disposal fee on new EEE products at the point of sale in Singapore, regardless how they are supplied.

sections.label: EPR framework for packaging waste
sections.summary: The Bill will lay the groundwork for an eventual EPR framework for packaging waste, noting Japan's excessive packaging despite its recycling attention.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Those who have visited Japan know that the Japanese, despite their attention to recycling, are completely buried in excessive packaging.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill will lay the groundwork for an eventual EPR framework for packaging waste.

sections.label: Food waste cut by planning
sections.summary: Good For Food has helped clients cut food waste by up to 30% to 40% through better planning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Good For Food has helped clients cut food waste by up to 30% to 40%, through better planning.

sections.label: Throwaway culture and underpricing
sections.summary: The throwaway culture exists because it is cheap, and underpricing and lack of regulation of unsustainable resources must stop.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The throwaway culture exists because it is cheap, Sir.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This basic underpricing and lack of regulation of unsustainable resources must stop.

sections.label: Cotton bag reuse estimate
sections.summary: The UK Environment Agency in 2006 estimated a cotton bag needs reuse 131 times in the best case to equal one single-use plastic bag.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The UK Environment Agency in 2006 estimated that a cotton bag requires reuse 131 times in the best case scenario to equal one single-use plastic bag.

sections.label: Price effect on personal behaviour
sections.summary: The speaker says for the rest of us it is a price effect, admitting personal failure to set an example and would do less if prices went up.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But for the rest of us, it is a price effect.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I admit to failing to set an example in how I live.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I may care about the environment but I drive, I fly and I use air-conditioning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would do this less if the prices went up.

sections.label: Building sustainable Singapore
sections.summary: The passage calls for building a sustainable Singapore without illusions on the nature of people and of markets.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us build a sustainable Singapore, without illusions on the nature of people and of markets.

sections.label: Climate change threats to Singapore
sections.summary: Climate change and rising sea levels are existential threats to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Climate change and rising sea levels are existential threats to Singapore.

sections.label: E-waste toxicity and recycling rates
sections.summary: Masagos Zukifli said e-waste is very toxic, and a UN report states only 20% is recycled while 80% is dumped in landfills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Minister Masagos Zukifli rightly pointed out, and I quote "e-waste is very toxic, people underestimate the toxicity of the e-waste that we dispose of and for the longest time we were not processing it." According to a United Nations (UN) report, only 20% of e-waste is recycled; 80% of e-waste is dumped in landfills.

sections.label: China's National Sword policy
sections.summary: Before 2018 most of the world's e-waste went to China, but China's National Sword policy began in early 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Prior to 2018, most of the world's e-waste ended up in China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, China's National Sword policy kicked in in early 2018.

sections.label: Plastic versus fish by 2050
sections.summary: According to the World Economic Forum, there will be more plastic than fish in the seas by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to the World Economic Forum, there will be more plastic than fish in our seas by the year 2050.

sections.label: Waste management technology for companies
sections.summary: Companies could develop technologies from biodegradable materials to distributed gasification systems, and mastering this can give Singapore businesses a competitive advantage globally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Can we encourage our companies to develop technologies to help to manage waste?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: These can range from better biodegradable materials to solutions to help manage waste at source, for example, distributed gasification system to treat waste locally at each HDB precinct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As the waste problem grows globally, mastering technology in this domain can create a competitive advantage for Singapore businesses looking to expand globally.

sections.label: Target for net negative waste
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Minister sets a target and suggests Singapore aim beyond zero waste to become a net negative waste nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister can set us a target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And I would like to humbly suggest that Singapore should aim to move one step beyond zero waste to become a net negative waste nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Through a combination of diplomacy, commerce and technology, we can help address an existential crisis for Singapore and for the world.

sections.label: Definition of larger sellers
sections.summary: The speaker calls the over-300-square-metre definition reasonable but asks MEWR to clarify whether large business-to-business and large online sellers qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The definition of larger sellers seems to be focused on larger retailers with more than 300 square metres of space, and this is a reasonable definition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, I would like MEWR to clarify whether large business-to-business sellers who carry a lot of volume directly to the businesses even though they do not have much retail space, do they qualify as large retailers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And whether large online sellers, such as Dell, Lazada, Alibaba or those e-shops within these platforms, are they included in this?

sections.label: Targeting food waste
sections.summary: The speaker is heartened that food waste is being targeted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, I am heartened to hear that we are targeting food waste.

sections.label: Fast fashion beyond the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government spurs efforts on fast fashion, which can last a few months but have long, destructive impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, I hope that the Government can spur efforts to look at another area beyond what is mentioned in the Bill today, and that is the area of fast fashion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fast fashion clothings can last for a mere few months, but its impact can be long and destructive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And to compound the challenge, consumers have difficulty gauging the impact of their actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is one clear area that our Government can work with environmentally conscious citizens.

sections.label: National spirit, three areas
sections.summary: The speaker calls this a manifestation of national spirit and hopes the Bill's three areas start more concrete steps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is a manifestation of our national spirit, of turning adversity into opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that the three areas that this Bill proposes will be the start of many more concrete and practical steps covering more areas.

sections.label: Pulau Semakau landfill running out
sections.summary: In 2035, sixteen years from now, the landfill Pulau Semakau will run out.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Sixteen years from now,	in 2035, our landfill Pulau Semakau will run out.

sections.label: Food waste recycled and generated
sections.summary: As of 2017, only 16% of food waste is recycled, while food waste is an estimated 10% of total waste generated.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: As of 2017, only 16% of our food waste is recycled while food waste alone accounts for an estimated 10% of total waste generated in Singapore.

sections.label: Food waste treatment mandate 2024
sections.summary: The Bill mandates that large hotels, malls and industrial food developments treat food waste from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Bill now mandates that large hotels, malls and industrial food developments need to treat food waste from 2024.

sections.label: E-waste framework support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the e-waste framework and is glad large retailers must provide in-store collection points.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I also strongly support the e-waste framework.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I am especially glad large retailers must now provide in-store collection points.

sections.label: Food waste recycling rate
sections.summary: Only 17% of the food waste generated gets recycled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The second worrying fact is that only 17% of the food waste that we generate gets to be recycled.

sections.label: Industry compliance deadline 2024
sections.summary: The industry needs to comply with the new requirement by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The industry needs to comply with this new requirement by 2024.

sections.label: Coordinated approach to food waste
sections.summary: An all-stakeholder coordinated approach is needed, and the speaker supports NEA's three-pronged strategy to reduce food waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, an all-stakeholder coordinated approach at every stage of the food cycle is needed to make a significant difference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I support NEA's three-pronged strategy to reduce food waste, that is, firstly, to prevent and reduce food wastage at its source; secondly, to redistribute unsold and excess food; and thirdly, to recycle and treat food waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Whilst today's Bill would in a large way address the food waste recycling and treatment issues, more can be done in the area of prevention and reduction of food waste, and I hope that the Government can play a more instrumental role here and continue to look at more game-changing policy measures to reduce food waste, working closely with the industries and community stakeholders.

sections.label: Food centre practices unchanged
sections.summary: Many people at food centres still do not practise the three suggestions, and the speaker urges the Government to step up the campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Many people that I saw at food centres continue to not practise the three suggestions mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There has been actually no noticeable impact, in my view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to do more and step up the campaign so that more people are conscious of this effort that we should do our part to reduce waste.

sections.label: Consultation with 250 companies
sections.summary: In developing the regulatory framework, economic agencies were worked with closely to consult over 250 companies and relevant stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First, in developing the regulatory framework, we have worked closely with our economic agencies to consult over 250 companies and relevant stakeholders.

sections.label: Thresholds exclude smaller producers
sections.summary: Thresholds exclude smaller producers from joining a PRS or reporting on packaging use, as regulations impact them more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Government regulations often impact these businesses more, as they are less able to benefit from economies of scale.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This is why, as asked by Mr Louis Ng, we have set thresholds to exclude smaller producers from joining a PRS or reporting on their packaging use.

sections.label: EEE producers joining PRS timeline
sections.summary: Producers of EEE who exceeded the threshold have up to six months to join PRS after registering and reporting put-to-market data to NEA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For example, producers of EEE who have exceeded the threshold will have up to six months to join PRS, after they have registered and reported their put-to-market data to NEA.

sections.label: NEA 2016 e-waste disposal study
sections.summary: NEA's 2016 study found only 6% of consumer e-waste is recycled, with the rest carted away, traded in, resold, donated or thrown away.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Based on NEA's 2016 study on e-waste disposal patterns, only 6% of our consumer e-waste is recycled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Thirty-five percent, comprising bulky e-waste, such as washing machines, is carted away by the deliverymen when new appliances are delivered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Twenty-four percent is traded in or resold; another 9% is donated; and the remaining 26% is simply thrown away.

sections.label: First three years collection targets
sections.summary: In the first three years, collection targets will be 60% of Large Household Appliances and 20% of other consumer products put-to-market by weight.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In the first three years, the collection targets will be 60% of Large Household Appliances and 20% of the other consumer products put-to-market by weight.

sections.label: No penalties first three years
sections.summary: As a transitional measure, penalties for missing collection targets will not be imposed on the PRS operator in the first three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As a transitional measure, penalties for missing collection targets will not be imposed on the PRS operator in the first three years.

sections.label: Requirements for packaged goods producers
sections.summary: Requirements will apply to brand owners, manufacturers, importers of packaged goods, and supermarkets with annual turnover over $10 million.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For a start, these requirements will apply to brand owners, manufacturers, importers of packaged goods, as well as supermarkets with an annual turnover of more than $10 million.

sections.label: Packaging EPR reporting requirements
sections.summary: Reporting requirements will cover about 4,500 medium and large enterprises putting packaging on the market, with exemption thresholds reviewed and an EPR framework for packaging including plastics by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The reporting requirements will cover about 4,500 medium and large enterprises in Singapore which put packaging on the market.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As we gain experience, we will review and adjust the exemption thresholds to ensure that these are meaningful and effective when we implement the EPR framework for packaging, including plastics, which will be put in place no later than 2025.

sections.label: Food waste segregation for large generators
sections.summary: The requirement to segregate and treat food waste will apply to hotels, malls and industrial developments that are large generators of food waste.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For a start, the requirement to segregate and treat food waste will apply to hotels, malls and industrial developments that are large generators of food waste.

sections.label: Onsite food waste treatment payback
sections.summary: A one-tonne per day onsite food waste treatment system typically has a five-year payback, and Grand Hyatt saves around $100,000 a year treating food waste into organic fertilisers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Typically, the payback period of a one-tonne per day onsite food waste treatment system is five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Grand Hyatt, for example, saves around $100,000 a year by treating its food waste into organic fertilisers for the hotel's landscaping purposes.

sections.label: No residential food waste rules
sections.summary: There are no plans to extend mandatory food waste segregation and treatment to residential areas, with regulatory measures focused on facilities that are large generators of food waste.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Assoc Prof Daniel Goh and Mr Christopher de Souza asked if we intend to extend mandatory food waste segregation and treatment to residential areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have no plans to do so and we will focus our regulatory measures on facilities that are large generators of food waste.

sections.label: Good Samaritan law consultations
sections.summary: SFA and NEA have been asked to conduct industry and public consultations to study a Good Samaritan law that could encourage donation of excess food to charities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As Ms Anthea Ong and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh said earlier, they both advocated having a Good Samaritan law, which could encourage the donation of excess food to charities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I have asked SFA and NEA to conduct industry and public consultations to study this further.

sections.label: REACH survey on plastic bags
sections.summary: A REACH survey on public sentiment towards disposable plastic bags showed 9% preferred a ban, 21% a charge and 69% greater public education to reduce usage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: A recent feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home (REACH) survey on public sentiment towards disposable plastic bags showed that 9% preferred a ban, 21% a charge and 69% preferred greater public education to reduce usage.

sections.label: Citizens' Workgroup on single-use plastics
sections.summary: A Citizens' Workgroup will be set up for Singaporeans to discuss tackling excessive consumption of single-use plastics, and NTUC FairPrice will run a plastic bag charge pilot.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We should take a pragmatic approach and find an inclusive solution that works for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This is why we have decided to set up a Citizens' Workgroup for Singaporeans from diverse backgrounds to come together to discuss and identify the way forward for us to collectively tackle the issue of excessive consumption of single-use plastics in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I note that NTUC FairPrice will run a one-month pilot to charge for plastic bags at seven of its outlets as well as undertake a consumer sentiment survey to gain insights on consumer behaviour.

sections.label: Resource Sustainability Bill milestone
sections.summary: The Resource Sustainability Bill is described as a major milestone in Singapore's sustainability journey and a pivotal framework for climate and environmental protection.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The Resource Sustainability Bill is a major milestone in Singapore's sustainability journey and a pivotal framework for climate and environmental protection.

sections.label: UK plastic bag charge decline
sections.summary: In the UK, a plastic bag charge led to an 80% decline in plastic bag use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Very often, we keep saying we need the plastic bags to bag our trash and the other countries do not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But in the UK, where after introducing a plastic bag charge, there was an 80% decline in the use of plastic bags.

sections.label: Workgroup and sustainability reporting coordination
sections.summary: A Workgroup will bring diverse people and views together, and the Monetary Authority of Singapore works with financial institutions and Singapore Exchange on sustainability reporting requirements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said, we are equally concerned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we want to form this Workgroup, bringing people from diverse backgrounds, diverse views together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Can I just check if the Ministry would be considering working with Singapore Exchange to integrate the reporting obligations that the Senior Minister of State has outlined in the Bill, with their sustainability reporting requirements?

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore continues to work with the financial institutions and, of course, with Singapore Exchange on sustainability reporting requirements and we will continue to also provide our support and work together with them on this.      .
